strengths: Strong theoretical framework with rigorous variational bounds (Theorems 3.1-3.2) that enable training-free posterior sampling without expensive retraining

Novel algorithmic contributions: quantized expectation enables differentiable optimization in discrete space via LFQ + STE; anchored remasking adapts adaptive decoding to leverage joint posterior confidence

Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 inverse problem tasks on FFHQ and ImageNet with consistent improvements (up to 31.36% LPIPS on SR), plus ablation studies demonstrating each component's contribution
Impressive computational efficiency: 66× shorter chains than pixel-space diffusion, 6× faster than PSLD at 512×512, enabling practical high-resolution inference (1024×1024 in 484s)
Excellent reproducibility: public datasets/base model, detailed algorithms, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, honest limitations discussion, and extensive appendix
Timely and well-motivated problem addressing discrete diffusion as foundation models emerge; advantages over continuous diffusion clearly articulated
weaknesses: Limited generalization scope: method heavily depends on MMaDA as base model; only one comparison with alternative (VQ-Diffusion, Table 5); unclear how approach performs with other discrete diffusion models; MMaDA's tokenizer acknowledged as having limited reconstruction quality

Theoretical gaps: Theorem 3.2's assumption that pretrained network 'closely approximates q(x)' not rigorously validated; no error analysis on bound tightness; straight-through estimator lacks theoretical justification for discrete case; no convergence guarantees for inner optimization loop

Hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc despite simplicity claims: beyond λp, method involves T=15 steps, M=100 iterations, η=1.0, VGG loss (λp=1e-3), noise σ=0.05, cosine schedule; only λp sensitivity analyzed; L1 vs L2 justified vaguely; no noise level sensitivity study

Fair comparison challenges: different base models (MMaDA vs CLIP-VAE latent), preprocessing via upsampling-downsampling makes isolating APS contribution difficult; limits conclusions about discrete vs continuous diffusion benefits

Incomplete analysis: limited ablation on codebook choice (binary vs continuous); missing analysis of when/why anchored remasking helps; minimal exploration of different measurement operators; no convergence analysis for inner loop; stylization only qualitatively evaluated

Baseline comparison limitations for discrete methods: only G2D2 and SGDD compared, with SGDD not evaluating all tasks; no comparison with other recent discrete work; questions about whether improvements are from APS or better MMaDA prior

Limited stylization evaluation: mostly qualitative; Table 3 shows mixed results vs continuous methods (ImageReward 0.63 vs RB-Modulation 1.18); no user studies; performance depends heavily on style descriptor quality

Generalization concerns: all inverse problems assume Gaussian likelihood; only natural images tested; failure cases (Figure 14) show struggles with out-of-distribution styles; unclear performance on medical imaging, satellite imagery, other domains

strengths: Addresses important gap in discrete diffusion posterior sampling with a principled training-free approach grounded in Theorems 3.1 and 3.3
Strong empirical results: consistent improvements over G2D2/SGDD (13.65-35.82% LPIPS gains) and competitive with continuous methods at 66× speedup (15 vs 1000 steps)
Comprehensive experimental validation: 6+ inverse problems, stylization, language modeling, extensive ablations (Figure 6), hyperparameter studies (Table 5), and large-scale evaluation (1000 samples)
Thorough presentation with detailed algorithms, full proofs, implementation details, and honest limitations discussion enabling reproducibility
Demonstrates strong generality: method works across diverse tasks and datasets (FFHQ, ImageNet) without task-specific tuning
Practical value of training-free inference without backpropagation through large foundation models
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: quantized expectation and anchored remasking are reasonable approximations but combine existing techniques (embeddings, LFQ, reweighting) without fundamentally new insights

Multiple stacked approximations inadequately characterized: first-order Taylor expansion (Eq. 8), stop-gradient treatment of Z_φ, and x^l substitution lack joint error analysis or empirical characterization of approximation quality
Theorem 3.3 assumes pretrained model closely approximates unconditional prior—verified empirically via reweighting but without formal theoretical justification of when this assumption breaks
Variational upper bound provides no quantification of gap to true posterior; unclear how loose the bound is in practice or how approximation quality varies across settings

Limited experimental scope in some evaluations: stylization has only 4 quantitative style-content pairs, QA benchmark contains 20 prompts, and some design choices lack ablations (anchor threshold schedule, loss function selection)
Dependence on discrete diffusion maturity: underlying MMaDA/MagVIT-v2 models still early-stage with limited tokenizer quality, currently underperforming continuous SOTA (Flux, SD3.5)
Missing analysis of key design elements: no convergence analysis despite Table 6, limited operator-dependence study beyond noise robustness, computational cost breakdown absent

strengths: First systematic treatment of posterior sampling for masked discrete diffusion models with purely discrete embeddings, addressing clear limitations of prior work (G2D2, SGDD)
Strong theoretical foundation with principled variational bounds (Theorems 3.1, 3.3) that motivate algorithmic choices and enable training-free inference by reusing pretrained models
Well-justified algorithmic innovations: quantized expectation reduces exponential O((2K)^L) complexity to O(KL), and anchored remasking motivated by posterior-aware token selection
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse tasks (linear/nonlinear inverse problems, stylization, QA) with rigorous ablations (§C.3) demonstrating 35.82% LPIPS and 10.94% PSNR improvements
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation (§C.1), complete pseudocode (Algorithm 1), hyperparameter studies (Table 5), builds on public codebase with public datasets
Practical efficiency: 66× shorter inference chain than continuous diffusion (DPS) with comparable or better quality, scales to 1024×1024 with only 15 steps
Honest limitations discussion (§C.10) with failure case analysis, acknowledging approximation nature and tokenizer quality constraints
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap underexplored: assumption that p_θ(x) closely approximates q(x) is never empirically verified; tightness of LAPS bound not analyzed; stop-gradient treatment of Z_φ diverges from theoretical assumptions

Quantized expectation approximation lacks formal error analysis: first-order Taylor expansion (Eq. C.5.1) ignores higher-order terms; 'local smoothness' assumption of A∘D never formalized; cumulative effect with straight-through estimator not quantified

Limited analysis of when/why method works: no characterization of which measurement operators or problem types favor APS; interplay between tokenizer quality and performance not experimentally isolated despite being noted as limitation
Stylization results underwhelming: modest improvements over base model (ImageReward 0.48→0.63), comparisons against older methods, strong dependence on style extractor quality not deeply analyzed
Question answering experiments underdeveloped: only 20 prompts, evaluation with lightweight models (0.6B reward, 8B judge), only two baselines, no analysis of which prompt types benefit from APS
Comparison fairness issues: different base models (VQ-Diffusion vs. MMaDA) across experiments; Table 7 identical-prior comparison limited to single task; some continuous baselines from 2022-2023

Missing ablations: necessity of perceptual loss not explicitly shown; sensitivity to reverse step count and remasking schedule not analyzed; computational cost-benefit of 100 optimization steps per timestep not detailed
